c01.summary.speaker: narrator
c01.summary.text: Alice follows a White Rabbit down a deep hole into a locked hall and changes size.

c01.goal.speaker: narrator
c01.goal.text: Unlock the tiny door, drink from the bottle, and eat the cake.

c01_b01.plain.speaker: narrator
c01_b01.plain.text: Alice sees a White Rabbit with a watch and follows it.

c01_b01.original.speaker: narrator
c01_b01.original.text: when the Rabbit actually took a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket, and looked at it, and then hurried on, Alice started to her feet, for it flashed across her mind that she had never before seen a rabbit with either a waistcoat-pocket, or a watch to take out of it, and burning with curiosity, she ran across the field after it, and fortunately was just in time to see it pop down a large rabbit-hole under the hedge.

c01_b02.plain.speaker: narrator
c01_b02.plain.text: Alice falls slowly down a very deep well.

c01_b02.original.speaker: narrator
c01_b02.original.text: The rabbit-hole went straight on like a tunnel for some way, and then dipped suddenly down, so suddenly that Alice had not a moment to think about stopping herself before she found herself falling down a very deep well.

c01_b03.plain.speaker: narrator
c01_b03.plain.text: She lands unhurt on sticks and leaves in a locked hall.

c01_b03.original.speaker: narrator
c01_b03.original.text: Alice was not a bit hurt, and she jumped up on to her feet in a moment: she looked up, but it was all dark overhead; before her was another long passage, and the White Rabbit was still in sight, hurrying down it.

c01_b04.plain.speaker: narrator
c01_b04.plain.text: She finds a tiny golden key that opens a small door.

c01_b04.original.speaker: narrator
c01_b04.original.text: However, on the second time round, she came upon a low curtain she had not noticed before, and behind it was a little door about fifteen inches high: she tried the little golden key in the lock, and to her great delight it fitted!

c01_b05.plain.speaker: narrator
c01_b05.plain.text: She sees a lovely garden, but she is too big to enter.

c01_b05.original.speaker: narrator
c01_b05.original.text: How she longed to get out of that dark hall, and wander about among those beds of bright flowers and those cool fountains, but she could not even get her head through the doorway

c01_b06.plain.speaker: narrator
c01_b06.plain.text: Alice drinks from a bottle and shrinks to ten inches high.

c01_b06.original.speaker: narrator
c01_b06.original.text: And so it was indeed: she was now only ten inches high, and her face brightened up at the thought that she was now the right size for going through the little door into that lovely garden.

c01_b07.plain.speaker: narrator
c01_b07.plain.text: She cannot reach the key on the table, so she eats cake.

c01_b07.original.speaker: narrator
c01_b07.original.text: Soon her eye fell on a little glass box that was lying under the table: she opened it, and found in it a very small cake, on which the words “EAT ME” were beautifully marked in currants.

item.pocket_watch.meaning.speaker: narrator
item.pocket_watch.meaning.text: The White Rabbit checks this watch because he is running late.

item.golden_key.meaning.speaker: narrator
item.golden_key.meaning.text: It unlocks the tiny door leading to the lovely garden.

item.drink_me_bottle.meaning.speaker: narrator
item.drink_me_bottle.meaning.text: Drinking from this bottle shrinks Alice to ten inches high.

line.alice.c01.1.plain.speaker: alice
line.alice.c01.1.plain.text: What is the use of a book without pictures?

line.alice.c01.1.original.speaker: alice
line.alice.c01.1.original.text: “and what is the use of a book,” thought Alice “without pictures or conversations?”

line.alice.c01.2.plain.speaker: alice
line.alice.c01.2.plain.text: I wonder how many miles I have fallen now?

line.alice.c01.2.original.speaker: alice
line.alice.c01.2.original.text: “I wonder how many miles I’ve fallen by this time?”

line.alice.c01.3.plain.speaker: alice
line.alice.c01.3.plain.text: I must be shutting up like a telescope.

line.alice.c01.3.original.speaker: alice
line.alice.c01.3.original.text: “What a curious feeling!” said Alice; “I must be shutting up like a telescope.”

line.alice.c01.4.plain.speaker: alice
line.alice.c01.4.plain.text: I will eat this cake to get into the garden.

line.alice.c01.4.original.speaker: alice
line.alice.c01.4.original.text: “Well, I’ll eat it,” said Alice, “and if it makes me grow larger, I can reach the key; and if it makes me grow smaller, I can creep under the door; so either way I’ll get into the garden, and I don’t care which happens!”

line.white_rabbit.c01.1.plain.speaker: white_rabbit
line.white_rabbit.c01.1.plain.text: Oh dear! Oh dear! I shall be late!

line.white_rabbit.c01.1.original.speaker: white_rabbit
line.white_rabbit.c01.1.original.text: “Oh dear! Oh dear! I shall be late!”

line.white_rabbit.c01.2.plain.speaker: white_rabbit
line.white_rabbit.c01.2.plain.text: Oh my ears and whiskers, how late it is getting!

line.white_rabbit.c01.2.original.speaker: white_rabbit
line.white_rabbit.c01.2.original.text: “Oh my ears and whiskers, how late it’s getting!”

c02.summary.speaker: narrator
c02.summary.text: Alice grows giant, cries a pool of tears, shrinks with a fan, and meets a Mouse.

c02.goal.speaker: narrator
c02.goal.text: Drop the fan to stop shrinking and swim to shore with the Mouse.

c02_b01.plain.speaker: narrator
c02_b01.plain.text: Alice grows more than nine feet tall and hits the roof.

c02_b01.original.speaker: narrator
c02_b01.original.text: Just then her head struck against the roof of the hall: in fact she was now more than nine feet high, and she at once took up the little golden key and hurried off to the garden door.

c02_b02.plain.speaker: narrator
c02_b02.plain.text: She cannot fit through the door and cries a big pool.

c02_b02.original.speaker: narrator
c02_b02.original.text: But she went on all the same, shedding gallons of tears, until there was a large pool all round her, about four inches deep and reaching half down the hall.

c02_b03.plain.speaker: narrator
c02_b03.plain.text: The startled White Rabbit drops his fan and white kid gloves.

c02_b03.original.speaker: narrator
c02_b03.original.text: The Rabbit started violently, dropped the white kid gloves and the fan, and skurried away into the darkness as hard as he could go.

c02_b04.plain.speaker: narrator
c02_b04.plain.text: Alice fans herself and shrinks down to two feet high.

c02_b04.original.speaker: narrator
c02_b04.original.text: She got up and went to the table to measure herself by it, and found that, as nearly as she could guess, she was now about two feet high, and was going on shrinking rapidly: she soon found out that the cause of this was the fan she was holding, and she dropped it hastily, just in time to avoid shrinking away altogether.

c02_b05.plain.speaker: narrator
c02_b05.plain.text: Alice slips into the pool of her own salty tears.

c02_b05.original.speaker: narrator
c02_b05.original.text: However, she soon made out that she was in the pool of tears which she had wept when she was nine feet high.

c02_b06.plain.speaker: narrator
c02_b06.plain.text: She meets a Mouse and scares it by talking about cats.

c02_b06.original.speaker: narrator
c02_b06.original.text: “Not like cats!” cried the Mouse, in a shrill, passionate voice. “Would you like cats if you were me?”

c02_b07.plain.speaker: narrator
c02_b07.plain.text: Alice, the Mouse, and other wet creatures swim to the shore.

c02_b07.original.speaker: narrator
c02_b07.original.text: Alice led the way, and the whole party swam to the shore.

item.rabbits_fan.meaning.speaker: narrator
item.rabbits_fan.meaning.text: Holding this fan makes Alice shrink rapidly.

item.white_kid_gloves.meaning.speaker: narrator
item.white_kid_gloves.meaning.text: The White Rabbit drops these tiny gloves in the hall.

line.alice.c02.1.plain.speaker: alice
line.alice.c02.1.plain.text: I am opening out like the largest telescope that ever was!

line.alice.c02.1.original.speaker: alice
line.alice.c02.1.original.text: “now I’m opening out like the largest telescope that ever was! Good-bye, feet!”

line.alice.c02.2.plain.speaker: alice
line.alice.c02.2.plain.text: Who in the world am I? That is the great puzzle!

line.alice.c02.2.original.speaker: alice
line.alice.c02.2.original.text: Who in the world am I? Ah, that’s the great puzzle!”

line.alice.c02.3.plain.speaker: alice
line.alice.c02.3.plain.text: O Mouse, do you know the way out of this pool?

line.alice.c02.3.original.speaker: alice
line.alice.c02.3.original.text: “O Mouse, do you know the way out of this pool? I am very tired of swimming about here, O Mouse!”

line.white_rabbit.c02.1.plain.speaker: white_rabbit
line.white_rabbit.c02.1.plain.text: Oh, the Duchess! She will be angry if I keep her waiting!

line.white_rabbit.c02.1.original.speaker: white_rabbit
line.white_rabbit.c02.1.original.text: “Oh! the Duchess, the Duchess! Oh! won’t she be savage if I’ve kept her waiting!”

line.white_rabbit.c02.2.plain.speaker: white_rabbit
line.white_rabbit.c02.2.plain.text: I must hurry along with these gloves and this fan.

line.mouse.c02.1.plain.speaker: mouse
line.mouse.c02.1.plain.text: Would you like cats if you were me?

line.mouse.c02.1.original.speaker: mouse
line.mouse.c02.1.original.text: “Would you like cats if you were me?”

line.mouse.c02.2.plain.speaker: mouse
line.mouse.c02.2.plain.text: Our family always hated cats: nasty, low, vulgar things!

line.mouse.c02.2.original.speaker: mouse
line.mouse.c02.2.original.text: Our family always hated cats: nasty, low, vulgar things!

line.mouse.c02.3.plain.speaker: mouse
line.mouse.c02.3.plain.text: Let us get to the shore, and I will tell my story.

line.mouse.c02.3.original.speaker: mouse
line.mouse.c02.3.original.text: “Let us get to the shore, and then I’ll tell you my history, and you’ll understand why it is I hate cats and dogs.”
